questions.question:
Which of the following statement/s is/are true?

I. 6³⁰⁰ > 16²⁰⁰

II. 4³⁰⁰ > 7²⁰⁰
questions.solution:
Statement I: 6³⁰⁰ > 16²⁰⁰

⇒ 6³⁰⁰ = (6³)¹⁰⁰ = 216¹⁰⁰

⇒ 16²⁰⁰ = (16²)¹⁰⁰ = 256¹⁰⁰

Hence 6³⁰⁰ > 16²⁰⁰ = 216¹⁰⁰ > 256¹⁰⁰ is false.

Statement II: 4³⁰⁰ > 7²⁰⁰

⇒ 4³⁰⁰ = (4³)¹⁰⁰ = 64¹⁰⁰

⇒ 7²⁰⁰ = (7²)¹⁰⁰ = 49¹⁰⁰

Hence 4³⁰⁰ > 7²⁰⁰ = 64¹⁰⁰ > 49¹⁰⁰ is true.

Hence only statement 2 is true.

questions.question: How many multiples of 3 are there from 1 to 100 which are not multiples of 2?
questions.solution:
We know that,

Number of terms = n = frac{{Last term - First term}}{{Difference between two terms}} + 1

The numbers between 1 to 100 which are multiple of 3 but not 2 are∶

⇒ 3, 9, 15, 21, …….., 99

 From above series, last term = 99, First term = 3 and Difference = 6

Rightarrow n = frac{{( {99 - 3} )}}{6} + 1

⇒ n = 16 + 1 = 17

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 5 days and A alone can do it in 30 days. B alone can do the work in how many days?
questions.solution:
Given,

A and B together can do a work in 5 days.

(A + B)’s one day work = 1/5

A can do the same work in 30 days.

A’s one day work = 1/30

Then,

B’s one day work = (A + B)’s one day work - A’s one day work

B’s one day work = 1/5 - 1/30 = (6 - 1)/30 = 5/30 = 1/6

Hence, B can do the same work = 6 days

questions.question: Three taps A, B and C can fill a tank in 10, 12 and 15 hours respectively. How long (in hours) would the three taps take to fill the tank if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
Given,

A can fill the tank in 10 hours.

∴ A’s one hour work = 1/10

B can fill the tank in 12 hours

∴ B’s one hour work = 1/12

C can fill the tank in 15 hours.

C’s one hour work = 1/15

Then, (A + B + C)’s one hour work = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = (6 + 5 + 4)/60 = 1/4

Hence, (A + B + C) can fill the tank in 4 hours.

questions.question: The marked price of a chair is Rs. 650 and a discount of 40% is given. What is the selling price (in Rs.) of the chair?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Marked price = Rs. 650 and Discount = 40%

Then, Selling price = MP - (MP × 40)/100 = 650 - (650 × 40)/100 = 650 - 260 = Rs. 390

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 840. A shopkeeper gives a discount of 40% and still makes a profit of 5%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Given,

MP = Rs. 840 and Discount% = 40%

Then,

SP = MP - (MP × 40)/100 = 840 - (840 × 40)/100 = 504

Now we have, SP = 504

Then, SP = CP + (CP × 5)/100 = CP(21/20)

⇒ CP = (504 × 20)/21 = 480

Hence, CP = Rs. 480

questions.question: If A ∶ B = 2 ∶ 3 and B ∶ C = 4 ∶ 5, then what is A ∶ B ∶ C?
The ratio of two numbers is 2 ∶ 5. If their difference is 36, then what is the smallest number?
questions.solution:
Given,

The ratio of two number is 2 ∶ 5.

Let the two numbers are 2x and 5x.

Difference = 5x - 2x = 36

⇒ 3x = 36

⇒ x = 12

The smallest number is 2x = 2 × 12 = 24

questions.question: The average of 23, 34, x, 21, 19 and 18 is 21. What is the value of x?
If the ratio of the cost price and selling price of an article is 5 ∶ 3, then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Given,

The ratio of the cost price and selling price of an article is 5 ∶ 3.

Let CP be 5x and SP be 3x

{{Loss \% }} = frac{{CP - SP}}{{CP}} times 100 = frac{{5x - 3x}}{{5x}} times 100 = 40\%

questions.question: A man gains 90% by selling an article for a certain price. If he sells it at half the price, then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price be x.

⇒ SP = CP + (CP × 90)/100 = x + 9x/10 = 19x/10

If he sells it at half the price, then SP = 19x/20

Loss % = frac{{CP - SP}}{{CP}} times 100 = frac{{x - frac{{19x}}{{20}}}}{x} times 100 = 5\%

questions.question: When 70 is subtracted from 25% of a number, the result is 20. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be x

According to question,

⇒ 25% of x - 70 = 20

⇒ x/4 = 90

⇒ x = 360

questions.question: If Q got 40% less marks than P, then the marks of P is how much percent more than that of Q?
questions.solution:
Let P gets x marks.

Then, Q = x - (40x/100) = 3x/5

Now we have, P = x and Q = 3x/5

Rightarrow frac{{{{P}} - {{Q}}}}{{{Q}}} times 100 = 66.66{{\% }}

questions.question: A person goes from point L to point M and comes back. His average speed for the entire journey is 50 km/hr. If his speed while going from L to M is 35 km/hr,then what will be the speed of the person (in km/hr) while coming back from M to L?
If 150 meters long train takes 10 seconds to cross a pole, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
Given,

The length of train = 150 m and Time =10 seconds

We know that,

Speed = Distance/Time = 150/10 = 15 m/s = 15 × 3600/1000 = 54 km/hr

questions.question: A certain principal invested in a scheme of compound interest. The amount obtained after 1 year is Rs. 3900 and the amount obtained after 2 years is Rs. 5070. What is the rate of interest (in percentage)?
In how many years, the number of students in college A is less than the average number of students in college B across all the years?
questions.solution:
Sum of student in college B = 784 + 820 + 846 + 856 + 912 + 900 = 5118

Average of student in college B = 5118/6 = 853

Number of students in college A in 2010 = 856 > 853

Number of students in college A in 2011 = 884 > 853

Number of students in college A in 2012 = 960 > 853

Number of students in college A in 2013 = 872 > 853

Number of students in college A in 2014 = 930 > 853

Number of students in college A in 2015 = 904 > 853

Hence, the number of students in college A is less than the average number of students in college B across all the years = 0

questions.question: What percentage of seats remained vacant in college B in 2015 if the capacity was 1000?
questions.solution:
Total capacity = 1000

Seats vacant = 1000 - 900 = 100

%vacant = (100 × 100)/1000 = 10%

questions.question: The difference between the number of students in both colleges is maximum in which year?
questions.solution:
Difference in 2010 = 856 - 784 = 72

Difference in 2011 = 884 - 820 = 64

Difference in 2012 = 960 - 846 = 114

Difference in 2013 = 872 - 856 = 16

Difference in 2014 = 930 - 912 = 18

Difference in 2015 = 904 - 900 = 4

Hence, the difference between the number of students in both colleges is maximum in 2012.

questions.question: What is the average difference of number of students in college A and B in the given period?
questions.solution:
Sum of student in college A = 856 + 884 + 960 + 872 + 930 + 904 = 5406

Average of student in college A = 5406/6 = 901

Sum of student in college B = 784 + 820 + 846 + 856 + 912 + 900 = 5118

Average of student in college B = 5118/6 = 853

Difference of average = 901 - 853 = 48
